fatal_errors: The proposed vapor-coating plus spark-plasma-sintering route does not reconstruct the central intervention: liquid-metal dealloying of a directionally segregated WTaVTi precursor in molten Cu.
It omits the selective Ti–Cu exchange, retention of a refractory-HEA ligament network, and formation of the approximately 300 nm W-rich passivating interlayer.

The stated 200–500 °C and 10–50 MPa boundary is unsupported and is not the reported 1200 °C, 96 h liquid-metal-dealloying condition; it is also generally inadequate as a complete SPS temperature specification for densifying W–Cu.
It does not address the required irradiation behavior or distinguish precursor-dendrite He-ion screening from testing of the finished composite.
No prior evidence is cited despite the explicit request for supporting evidence.
Mechanical durability is asserted even though no quantitative mechanism, target, or relevant durability test is supplied.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes the broad W–Cu contact and porosity problem and proposes measurements of thermal conductivity, strength, and microstructure. However, it largely combines fabrication approaches already mentioned in the prompt rather than identifying the target liquid-metal-dealloying strategy. It misses the WTaVTi precursor, directional sacrificial Ti/V-rich channels, bicontinuous RHEA–Cu architecture, W-rich interfacial layer, 1200 °C/96 h treatment, temperature-dependent thermal crossover, and qualified He-irradiation result. Its casting baseline is poorly matched because the prompt already states that conventional casting cannot readily produce uniform W–Cu. The falsification experiment is only generic: it lacks matched specimens, numerical acceptance criteria, irradiation controls, interface/composition diagnostics, and service-relevant thermal cycling or durability observations. With no evidence and implausibly underspecified processing boundaries, the proposal is not adequately supported as an alternative.
